name: taste-skill
tagline: A design skill that gives your AI coding agent good taste - it stops building generic, boring-looking interfaces.
sentence: Install taste-skill and the websites, apps and dashboards your AI agent builds look designed - with real visual hierarchy, spacing and motion, not the usual flat gray default.

visual.alt: A botanical website called Floria with the heading 'Botanic Architecture': product cards at $95-$185 with plant images, process steps (Soil Mapping, Growth Protocol, Root Cultivation, Bloom Optimization), and an archives section - all with polished typography and warm earth tones.
visual.caption: A website built by an AI agent with taste-skill installed: real layout, hierarchy and typography instead of generic defaults.

board.say: Your AI coding agent builds working interfaces, but they all look the same - flat, gray, generic. They work, but nobody would call them well-designed.
board.eg: You ask Claude Code to build a landing page and get a technically correct page with default fonts, no visual hierarchy and the same layout every AI produces.

board.say: You install taste-skill and it guides your AI agent's design decisions automatically.
board.eg: Install the skill once, and every UI your agent builds benefits from design guidance - no extra prompting needed.

board.say: Your usual request to the AI agent - build a page, design a dashboard, create a form - but now with design guidance applied.
board.eg: The same prompt you always use: 'Build a landing page for a coffee shop.' The skill adds design taste to the output.

board.say: It loads design principles into the agent's context, guiding choices about layout, typography, color, spacing and motion.
steps: The skill loads with adjustable dials: DESIGN_VARIANCE (how bold), MOTION_INTENSITY (how much animation), VISUAL_DENSITY (how packed)
It guides the agent's choices: typography pairings, color palettes, spacing scales, visual hierarchy and layout structure
The agent applies these principles to whatever it builds - pages, dashboards, forms, components
board.eg: The README's Floria example: instead of a generic plant shop page, the agent builds a page with 'Botanic Architecture' branding, warm earth tones, product cards at real prices, and a polished process section.

board.say: UIs that look designed, not generated - with real visual hierarchy, spacing and polish.

outputs.eg: A landing page with thoughtful typography, color and layout - not the flat gray default
Dial DESIGN_VARIANCE up for bold, creative layouts or down for conservative, corporate ones

before: Every AI-built interface looks the same: default fonts, flat gray palette, no visual hierarchy. They work, but they look like AI made them.
Getting better design from an AI agent means writing long, detailed design prompts every time.
after: Install once and every UI the agent builds gets design guidance - real typography, color, spacing and hierarchy.
Tune the output with three dials: how bold, how animated, how dense. No design prompts needed.

steps: Install taste-skill in your AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or others): follow the instructions at [tasteskill.dev](https://tasteskill.dev).
Ask your agent to build a landing page for a fictional business (like 'a specialty coffee roaster called Evergreen'). Look at the typography, colors and layout.
Try adjusting the DESIGN_VARIANCE dial (in the skill's settings) from low to high and rebuild the same page to see the difference.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill

If that scan passes: install taste-skill, build a landing page for a fictional coffee roaster, then adjust DESIGN_VARIANCE from low to high and rebuild to see the difference. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No data found for exact install size. It is a skill (a set of design guidelines loaded into the agent's context), not a standalone application.
footprint.memory: No data found. Runs as a skill inside your AI coding agent.
footprint.runs_on: Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other AI coding agents. No specific hardware requirements.

best_for: You use an AI coding agent to build UIs and want them to look designed, not generated - with real typography, color and hierarchy
You are not a designer and want one-click design improvement without learning design principles yourself
skip_if: You are a professional designer who sets your own design system - a generic taste skill may conflict with your brand guidelines
You only build backend code or APIs - taste-skill helps with visual interfaces, not server logic

alternatives.name: impeccable
alternatives.line: Another design skill for AI agents. Different design philosophy - impeccable focuses on 'design sense' while taste-skill focuses on 'good taste.'

alternatives.name: ui-ux-pro-max
alternatives.line: A design playbook for AI agents focused on professional web and mobile screens. More structured and rule-based than taste-skill.

watch: **By Leon Lin, a solo developer.** 175 commits, MIT license. The skill is small and focused, but maintenance depends on one person.
**Works with multiple agents, not just Claude Code.** taste-skill supports Codex, Cursor and other AI coding agents. Your mileage may vary by agent.
**Design is subjective.** The 'taste' this skill teaches is one person's design philosophy. It improves generic output significantly, but may not match your brand or aesthetic.
**Already on the Category Radar.** taste-skill has been in our Design and Branding lane since October 2. It earned this feature through sustained growth, not a spike.
